name: [Equip] Gemini spend jumped
message:
Billed output tokens crossed 500k in an hour.

That is more than a whole 870-field course (roughly 400k output tokens all in) produced inside sixty minutes, and several times anything production has actually done. Three explanations, in order of likelihood:

1. **The model changed.** A thinking model spends ~840 hidden tokens per string and bills them as output — six times the answer. Check GEMINI_MODEL *and* GEMINI_REVIEW_MODEL against MEASURED_GEMINI_MODELS in app/core/config.py; the backend logs a warning at boot, naming the setting and quoting the measured models' prices, when either is running an unmeasured model. GEMINI_REVIEW_MODEL is not set in Vercel at all — it runs on the code default, so a code change moves it with nothing in the environment to compare against.
2. **A loop.** A job re-translating the same course, or the sweep queueing a course it can never complete. Check /api/v1/admin/translations/queue-status for a course with climbing attempts.
3. **Real work.** A bulk import or a newly switched-on language. Legitimate — and worth knowing about anyway.

@arvavitcorp@gmail.com

WHY THIS NUMBER. The threshold was 2M/h when this file was written, chosen from nothing. Measured against the metric on 2026-08-19: the busiest eight-hour window in thirty days produced 92,478 output tokens in total, so 2M could not have fired on any event short of a catastrophe, including the very model regression the monitor exists to catch. 500k critical is above every legitimate hour on record with room for one large course, and 250k warning is roughly three times the busiest hour ever observed.

NOTE: thinking tokens are billed as output and are NOT in this sum. `equip.gemini.tokens_thinking_total` is emitted by the backend but has no log-based-metric rule in Datadog, so it does not exist as a metric and a query summing it returns nothing at all — verified again on 2026-08-19 — which is why this monitor counts output alone. `docs/datadog/README.md` has the recipe for creating the rule; add it, then add the term back and raise both thresholds by the measured thinking ratio.

NOTE ON WHAT THIS NOW COUNTS. Until 2026-08-20 this sum saw the translator only: the review call emitted no token metrics at all, while running gemini-3.5-flash-lite at $0.30/M in and $2.50/M out — 3x and 6.25x the translator — and accounting for roughly 52% of a full rebuild's cost. Half the bill was outside the metric this monitor is built on. The reviewer now reports its tokens under model:gemini-3.5-flash-lite and role:review, so the series is wider than the history the thresholds above were calibrated against. The reviewer answers a JSON verdict capped at 512 output tokens, so the expected effect is roughly a doubling: the busiest eight-hour window on record (92,478 output tokens) would read around 185k, still under the 250k warning. That is an estimate, not a measurement — re-derive both thresholds from a week of the widened series.
